messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `canary-healthcheck-prod-eu` (alert_id=PD-9987) - threshold breached (error rate > 5%)

pagerduty: Pager PD-9987: Triggered -> NOT_ACKED (details: https://pd.redwood.example/incidents/PD-9987)

sophia: saw the page. I'm on it, pulling the canary dashboard now.

raj: also saw it. are we seeing any customer errors or just synths?

sophia: initial glance: only synthetic checks failing. no 5xx spikes in prod, but the canary agent's latencies are high and many probes returning 502-like wrappers.

sophia: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/canary-prod?panelId=3 - 95p latency jumped from ~60ms to ~1.2s across eu hosts starting 15:08 UTC

sophia: running quick probe from floater box:
```
curl -vv "https://canary-prober-eu.redwood.internal/health?probe=api" -H "X-Probe: smoke" -w "
status:%{http_code} time:%{time_total}
"
```

ops-lead: getting the same from my shell: a bunch of timeouts and intermittent 502s. could be a backend pool exhaustion or a routing flap.

raj: acking the PD page so it stops paging while we triage.

pagerduty: PD-9987 acknowledged by raj at 2024-05-03T15:12:38Z

sophia: thanks. quick checklist:
- check canary prober host health (cpu/mem/io)
- check prober-sidecar logs for 503/connection refused
- check upstream routing (edge LB -> probe agent)
- confirm whether this is a single availability zone or multi-AZ

sophia: `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/canary-prober --since=10m` shows repeated `connection reset by peer` and `read timeout` from the prober to `prober-service`

raj: i'm sshing to the prober pod to inspect FD counts and kube-proxy. might be ephemeral port exhaustion on the node.

(taylor joined the thread)

taylor: chiming in. if it's port exhaustion we're seeing, restarting the prober pod or rolling the daemonset usually clears it. can we do a controlled restart?

sophia: good idea. before restart, let's toggle probe fanout to single-host mode to avoid flooding:
```
# run from ops-toolbox
redwoodctl canary update --region eu --fanout 1
```

ops-lead: on it, setting fanout=1 and muting the PD rule for 30m to avoid noisy repeats while we investigate. will annotate PD: "investigating, muting for 30m"

ops-lead: fanout set to 1 -> verified. PD rule muted for 30 minutes.

sophia: restarting canary-prober pods (graceful).
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/canary-prober
```

sophia: pods are coming back up, initial probe success rate improving from 60% -> 98% on the node I checked.

raj: on the node I inspected, ephemeral port usage was at 95% due to a leak in `sidecar-net` version 1.2.3. there are many TIME_WAIT sockets accumulating. kernel params seem default.

raj: workaround: rotated the prober pods and bumped `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` temporarily to broaden ephemeral ports. patching to fix sidecar in staging ASAP.

ops-lead: created incident ticket INC-2024-245: "Canary prober port exhaustion -> noisy PD pages". assigned to eng-sre. link: https://tickets.redwood.example/INC-2024-245

sophia: customer impact assessment: no direct user-visible errors found in production metrics or customer error dashboards. the issue impacted synthetic checks and our alerting path only. marking customer_impact = none for now, will update if we see any downstream regressions.

taylor: suggest we add a temporary suppression rule to only page on sustained failures across 3 consecutive canary waves instead of immediate single-wave pages; reduces noise. will draft change.

raj: opened a PR to update sidecar image to 1.2.4 which contains the socket leak fix. CI passing. linking: https://git.redwood.example/infra/sidecar/merge_requests/458

incident-bot: Reminder: PD-9987 was muted by ops-lead (30m) - will unmute at 2024-05-03T15:42:00Z unless extended.

sophia: next steps:
- merge sidecar fix and schedule canary rollout (raj)
- add 3-wave suppression to PD rule (taylor)
- write short runbook entry for prober debug + fanout toggle (sophia)
- follow-up postmortem only if customer impact appears (ops-lead)

taylor: i'll take the handoff for the next 2 hours to keep an eye on reoccurrence.

raj: I'll coordinate the sidecar rollout; target a staged rollout across eu nodes in next 30m.

ops-lead: good. leaving this thread open while we watch. if anything escalates, re-enable immediate paging. otherwise we'll close after 2h stable. :thumbsup:

sophia: noting runtime metrics snapshot for post-incident notes:
- canary failure window: 15:07 - 15:16 UTC
- peak probe error rate: 7.3%
- successful mitigation: fanout -> 1, pod restarts, ephemeral port range bump

pagerduty: PD-9987 -> RESOLVED (muted and acknowledged, automated unmute scheduled)

incident-bot: thread note: handoff -> taylor (15:20 UTC). will auto-close thread if no activity until 17:20 UTC.

sophia: thanks team. leaving detailed artifacts in the ticket INC-2024-245.

taylor: will follow up with a short blameless note tomorrow.

ops-lead: closing loop for now. reopen if we see replays. :white_check_mark:
